items.item: Server is the only writer of Gold; client never sends amounts or prices
Validates remote arguments (types, NaN/inf, bounds) and rate-limits shop requests
Avoids yields between balance check and deduction (atomic spend)
Persistence handled safely (UpdateAsync or session-locked profile; load-before-play; BindToClose)
Does not treat leaderstats as source of truth
Kill rewards awarded by server-side kill attribution, not a client 'I killed X' remote

incorrect_or_stale: Ships a broken/confusing DataService.Loaded stub (assigns a BindableEvent, then overwrites it with a table) and patches it afterward in prose instead of fixing the code
BindToClose uses a fixed task.wait(5) instead of waiting for saves to finish, so saves can be cut off
A player who leaves during load never has the lock released, so their profile stays locked for up to 90s
Saves on leave or autosave don't retry or serialize, so saves can overlap or be lost silently
slop: Generic 'consider ProfileService/ProfileStore' and 'ProcessReceipt must be idempotent' advice tacked on at the end

incorrect_or_stale: --!strict code (e.g. setmetatable cast, untyped 'unknown' params) likely produces type-check errors as written
slop: Meaningless 'Apex: security → data → networking' header and a meta note about having no file-write tool
Gold-per-minute telemetry and transaction-log suggestions are generic follow-ups
overengineering: Token-bucket rate limiter where a simple debounce would do
A separate Studio dev datastore plus a per-player inflight save serialization loop goes beyond the 'concise' request

raw.reason: Both get the core security right, but B's persistence is more correct (it releases the lock if a player leaves mid-load, serializes and retries saves, kicks on a lost lock, and waits for saves in BindToClose), while A ships a broken Loaded stub and has weaker shutdown and lock handling; A's kill attribution is a bit more concrete.
